intro: Date Info takes any date you enter and shows its calendar details: the weekday, the day of the year, the ISO week number, the calendar quarter, whether it falls in a leap year, and how many days are in that month. It's handy when you need quick date facts like the ISO week or day-of-year without pulling out a calendar or writing throwaway code. All calculations use UTC and run instantly in your browser.
useCases: Look up the ISO 8601 week number for a given date when scheduling or labeling reports
Find the day-of-year (1-365/366) for date math or log filenames
Check which calendar quarter (Q1-Q4) a date falls into for financial or reporting periods
Confirm whether a year is a leap year before validating February dates
Get the number of days in a specific month for billing or calendar logic
Quickly identify the weekday for a past or future date

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Date Info runs entirely in your browser and nothing you type is uploaded or stored on any server. The site is fully client-side and open source, so you can verify this yourself.

faq.q: What date formats can I enter?
faq.a: Any string that JavaScript's Date constructor accepts, such as ISO 8601 (2026-06-08), full date-times, or formats like "June 8, 2026". If the value can't be parsed it reports "Invalid date."

faq.q: Does it use my local timezone or UTC?
faq.a: All output is computed in UTC. A date without a time component is treated as midnight UTC, so the weekday and day-of-year reflect the UTC date rather than your local one.

faq.q: How is the week number calculated?
faq.a: It uses the ISO 8601 week definition, where weeks start on Monday and the week containing the year's first Thursday is week 1. This can differ from week-numbering schemes that start the week on Sunday.
For each valid date it shows the weekday, day of year, ISO week number, calendar quarter, whether the year is a leap year, and the number of days in that month.
